This house is not the Burrow. This house is where we wait.

The Great Ones do not live here. They live %2 of this place,

For servers that want to decide where their sewers begin. Open: anybody can climb down any manhole cover, trapdoor or storm-drain grate that leads to the sewers. Closed: nobody can, until an admin opens one (right-click it as an admin). Either way an admin can open or close any one of them, admins themselves can always climb down, and a ladder always takes a player back up. In single player there is no admin: leave this on Open.
How many of the cult's dead are in their temple under the fields. They are put down the first time each part of it is walked into, so parts already found are not affected.

Whether players can widen the sewers. With a pickaxe or a sledgehammer, a square of rock can be dug out or a tunnel wall knocked through. With explosives, a bomb that goes off below ground opens the rock round it.
Who fits through a kerb drain
Only the slim and lightly loaded

A kerb drain is narrower than a manhole. Anybody: no limit. Not the overweight or overloaded: nobody whose character has the High Weight or Very High Weight trait goes down one, and nobody carrying more than they can carry (the Weighed Down moodle) goes down or comes up one. Only the slim and lightly loaded: the same, and nobody carrying more than half of what they can carry. Manhole covers, trapdoors and outfalls are never limited. Takes effect at once.

The iron grates at the kerbs of the game's own streets. Yes: one near a tunnel is a narrow way down into the sewers. No: they are bolted down, and nobody but an admin goes down one. A ladder under one always takes a player back up. Takes effect at once.

The EXIT stencils and arrows painted on the tunnel walls near the ladders. None: find your own way out (the sewer map still shows every ladder you have used). Few: about one in three. By every ladder: all of them. Only tunnels not yet opened up are affected.

Some narrow culverts, well away from the ladders, hold foul air behind the county's warning placards. Breathe it without a gas mask or respirator and you get sick. Mild: queasy at worst. Harmful: sick, and it costs health while you stay. Deadly: stay and it kills. A mask with a filter keeps it out, and uses the filter up.

Some garages, kitchens and storerooms have a trapdoor in the floor, and a ladder down to the sewer under the street. No: none is put into a house nobody has been near yet, for servers where a player's house should have no back door. Trapdoors already there stay.

The brick labyrinth under the deep woods west of Muldraugh. No: its trapdoor and the hut over its way out are not put in, so nobody finds a way down, and its annotated map is not handed out. If they are already there, they stay.
How much is in a shelter's or hideout's crates and shelves when you first find them. Journals and sewer plans are there whatever this is set to. Only places not yet found are affected.
How many of those who went in before are still walking its corridors: about a thousand when set to All. Fewer is kinder to a busy server. Only corridors nobody has walked yet are affected.

Only for when another mod has something in the same ground. This is the square of the labyrinth's trapdoor, counted east; the next setting is the same square counted south. The whole labyrinth, 256 squares a side, lies south-east of it and moves with it, in steps of 8 squares. Choose empty ground far from every town, and set it before the world is made: what is already built stays where it is.
See the setting above. The mod's own place is 8922 east, 10322 south.

Under Louisville a false wall of loose bricks hides the nest of the rodents of unusual size, and their hoard. Open: whoever finds the wall can pull it down. Sealed: the bricks do not come away, for a server keeping the nest for later. A wall already pulled down stays down.
The iron grates in the banks of the river, the creeks and the lakes: ways into the sewers away from the streets. No: none is put into a bank nobody has been near yet. Grates already there stay.

Mostly ordinary: sewer workers, drifters and townsfolk; hardly any carry a bag. Mixed: some came down with a pack. Survivors: many did, and their bags are full (the mod's balance before 0.3.2). Only tunnels not yet opened up are affected.
Longest passage to a new way down
When an admin puts a way down on a street, a passage is dug from its foot to the nearest tunnel. This is how far away that tunnel may be.

How many of the game's own rats are down there when a stretch of tunnel is first opened up. They can be trapped, and eaten if you are hungry enough. The rodents of unusual size in the nest under Louisville are there whatever this is set to.

How much of a beating each of the rodents in the nest takes. Weak: two blows of any weapon, or one bullet. Normal: three blows, or two bullets. Tough: six blows, or four bullets. Monstrous: twelve blows, or eight bullets. A shove throws one back whatever this is set to.

Whether zombies on one side of the street's surface come to a player on the other. No: footsteps, digging and gunfire in the sewer draw nobody on the street, a player on the street draws nobody in the sewer, and a zombie that was chasing you gives up when you climb down or out; the dead on your own level hear and see you as well as ever. Yes: the game's own rule, where a floor stops no sound, and running under a street brings its dead to stand over you.
How many zombies are down there when a stretch of tunnel is first opened up. Shelters that were someone's last stand keep their occupants whatever this is set to.
